Run a pipeline over a set of recordings

Source: R/runPipeline.R
runPipeline.Rd

Runs a pipeline() on every file of a RecordingSet and writes its results to a folder, the store. The store is the whole state of a run, so the same call made again carries on where the last one stopped, and the results are read back with pipelineResults().

Usage

runPipeline(
  p,
  set,
  store,
  batch = 1000,
  max.memory = 4e+09,
  keep = NULL,
  retry = FALSE,
  cl = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

p

A Pipeline.

set

A RecordingSet.

store

The folder to write the results to. It is made if it does not exist.

batch

How many files to run between writes to the store.

max.memory

The most memory, in bytes, a file may take once decoded to be read whole, 4 GB unless it is given, or Inf to read every file whole.

keep

A folder to keep downloaded files in, or NULL to delete each one once it has been run. Each file is kept in a folder of its own, named from its URL, so that files of the same name from different places are kept apart, and one already there is not downloaded again.

retry

If TRUE, files that failed in an earlier run are run again.

cl

A cluster from the parallel package, to run batches on, or NULL.

quiet

If TRUE, no progress is reported.

Value

The set, invisibly, with the hash of every file the store holds filled in where the set gave none, so that its rows can be joined to the results by hash.

Files

The recordings of a set that share a hash or a location are one file, as a recording the Animal Sound Archive lists under three species is, and each file is run once. A file is fetched from its location: a local file is read where it is, and one at a URL is downloaded, then deleted once it has been run unless keep names a folder to keep it in. Each file is read by readAudio(), whole unless it is too long to hold (see Long files), tagged with its location as its origin and with the columns of the set that all of its recordings agree on, such as start, lat and lon, in the "recordingSet" entry of its metadata, and measured by calculateMetadata(). Columns its recordings disagree on, such as the taxon of a file listed under three species, are left in the set.

A file is known by the SHA-256 hash of its bytes. A file the set gives a hash has to match it, and a local file the set gives none is hashed before the run starts, so that a file already in the store is recognised wherever it has been moved to, and copies of one file are run once. A file that cannot be hashed then is left to fail when it is read. A file at a URL the set gives no hash is recognised by its location once it has been run. A local location is made absolute before the run, as a worker of a cluster can be working in another folder.

Long files

A file is read whole unless it would take more than max.memory bytes once decoded, which is worked out from its header before it is read. R holds a sample in 4 bytes for a RIFF WAV file of 8, 16 or 32-bit PCM, for an AudioMoth triggered recording, and for an MP3 file, and in 8 for a WAV file of 24-bit PCM or floating-point audio and for anything the av package decodes, a WAV file in the RF64 or BW64 form and FLAC among them. A triggered recording is measured as it will be once expanded.

A file over max.memory is read a window at a time, by each windowing() at the top of the pipeline, as windowing() reads a file. Each window holds the samples, and the tags, of the window cut from the whole recording, so the results are those a whole read gives, and the wave_hash of the file is taken a block at a time. That writes the samples to a temporary file, as the digest is of all of them at once, so it needs room on disk for 8 bytes a sample while it is taken, and for a file of more than two channels, whose channels are written apart and then joined, 8 bytes more for each sample of one channel. Only a RIFF WAV file of PCM or floating-point audio can be read in parts that are exact, so any other file over max.memory, an MP3 or a FLAC file among them, fails without being read, as does a triggered recording, which is expanded whole. So does a file whose pipeline has a step outside a windowing given then=, which needs the whole recording at once, or windows that are themselves over max.memory. The size of a file other than a WAV file is asked of the av package, and where that is not installed such a file is read whole.

Batches

The files not yet in the store are run in batches of batch files, and each batch is written to the store once all of its files have been run. Stopping a run loses only the batch it was in, and the next run starts again from that batch. With cl, a cluster from the parallel package, each worker runs whole batches and writes them itself, and needs this package installed.

Failures

A file that cannot be fetched or read, that does not match the hash the set gives it, or on which a step fails, is recorded as failed with the reason, and the run moves on. It has a row in every table of results, with error saying what went wrong, and it is not run again unless retry is TRUE.

The store

The store holds a folder for each pipeline run into it, named by the pipeline's id, so pipelines that share a store are kept apart and a file is run once for each of them. That folder holds the pipeline itself, in pipeline.rds, and a batches folder with a list of the files each batch covered and a file for each of its tables of results, so that one table can be read without the others. As the id covers the code of every package a step uses, a pipeline run after any of them has changed is run into a folder of its own.

See also

pipeline() to write one, and pipelineResults() to read what a run wrote.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Working out a pipeline's id hashes the code of every package it uses,
# which takes some seconds.
f <- system.file("extdata", "AUDIOMOTH.WAV", package="sonicscrewdriver")
set <- recordingSet(f, source="AudioMoth")
p <- pipeline(windowing(1, time.unit="seconds", then=dutyCycle()))
store <- file.path(tempdir(), "store")
set <- runPipeline(p, set, store)
res <- pipelineResults(store, p)
head(res[[1]])
merge(res[[1]], set, by.x="file", by.y="hash")[, c("window_start", "value", "uri")]
} # }
